questions.question: Which statement describes the consumption-based model?

options.text: You pay a fixed price for hardware before using it
options.why: That is capital expenditure, the opposite.

options.text: You pay only for the resources you use
options.why: Correct. Usage is metered and billed.

options.text: All cloud services are free up to unlimited usage
You pay the same monthly amount regardless of usage
options.why: That describes a flat fee, not consumption pricing.

questions.explanation: The consumption-based model bills you for what you actually use.

questions.question: Which TWO are benefits of the consumption-based model?

options.why: Bills vary with usage under consumption pricing.

options.text: Ability to stop paying for resources you no longer need
options.why: Correct. Delete or scale down to reduce cost.

options.text: Customers must buy their own hardware

questions.explanation: No up-front cost and paying only while you need resources are core benefits.

questions.scenario: A developer shuts down Windows from inside an Azure VM. The VM shows as 'Stopped' in the portal, not 'Stopped (deallocated)'.
questions.question: Will compute charges continue?

options.text: Yes. The VM is still allocated, so compute charges continue
options.why: Correct. Only deallocated VMs stop compute billing.

options.text: No. All charges stop when the OS shuts down
options.why: The hardware is still reserved, so compute is billed.

options.text: No. Azure never charges for VMs
options.why: Running and allocated VMs are billed.

questions.explanation: Stop the VM from Azure (portal, CLI, PowerShell) to deallocate it and stop compute charges. Disk charges continue.

questions.question: Which type of data transfer is generally free in Azure?

options.why: Correct. Inbound data transfer is generally not charged.

options.text: Data transferred out to the internet (egress)
options.why: Outbound data transfer is generally charged.

options.text: All data transfer is always charged

questions.explanation: Ingress is generally free; egress and inter-region transfer usually incur charges.
